first.rationale: Two of the three current problems (activation down 6%, onboarding completion down 4%) are internal funnel issues directly addressed by prior positive results in memory_31 (signup simplification lifted SMB activation) and memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value). These are plausibly linked—onboarding friction likely drives part of the activation decline—so a single experiment tightening onboarding could move both metrics at once, which is the best use of one experimental slot. I want to verify these two records before committing, since 'durable lift' claims need checking against original sample size/segment to make sure the effect wasn't SMB-only or short-lived, especially since current dips may stem from a different cause (e.g., competitor pull) than what the earlier experiments addressed. I am deliberately NOT choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor threat: matching aggressive entry pricing risks attracting low-LTV, price-sensitive accounts and eroding sustainable qualified revenue (the stated objective), and memory_73 alone doesn't tell us about long-term retention/margin effects of a reactive price cut under competitive pressure — that's a different causal context than the original experiment. I'm flagging this as an unresolved downstream value risk that still needs attention, possibly next cycle, rather than assuming it's safely deferred. Scale is a standard experiment rather than broad rollout because we're re-validating a previously good lever under new conditions (competitive market shift), not blindly scaling a stale result.

mid.rationale: Archive confirms both records with real caveats worth respecting rather than smoothing over. exp_31 (signup simplification) shows activation +9% and qualified revenue +4%, but also a -1% dip in 30-day retention, and explicitly did not replicate outside SMB — so this lever should not be broadened past self-serve/SMB accounts on the strength of this record alone. exp_86 (shortened onboarding) is cleanly confirmed with completion +13%, time-to-value improved, and retention +3%, with no equivalent scope caveat. Combined, they directly target the two internally-caused metrics currently declining (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%), and their mechanisms are complementary (fewer signup fields feeding into a shorter onboarding flow), making a joint onboarding-simplification experiment the highest-leverage use of the single slot this week. I'm scaling this as a standard experiment rather than broad rollout because exp_31's segment limitation and retention dip mean we should re-validate combined effects before wide deployment, and because current market conditions (competitor pricing pressure) differ from the original experiment context, so a fresh read is warranted rather than assuming an old durable lift generalizes unchanged today. I continue to flag downstream value risk on two fronts: (1) exp_31's minor retention cost could compound if stacked with a separately shortened flow, and (2) the competitor's aggressive SMB pricing is an unaddressed external threat that this experiment doesn't answer — deferring promotional_pricing is a deliberate tradeoff given the one-slot constraint and the objective of sustainable qualified revenue, not evidence that the pricing threat is resolved or safe to ignore next cycle.

final2.rationale: The situation has materially changed since my earlier decision: a second, deeper competitor price cut plus doubled churn conversations in price-sensitive SMB accounts is now an acute, external revenue-threatening event, not the internal funnel softness that simplify_onboarding was designed to address. Onboarding fixes act on activation/completion mechanics and will not stop active SMB accounts from leaving for cheaper alternatives this week; they solve a different problem on a different timescale. Given leadership needs a response today and the risk is concentrated and immediate, I'm switching this cycle's action to promotional_pricing, informed by memory_73 (targeted promotional pricing was effective for price-sensitive SMB with strong acquisition and revenue lift). However, I could not verify memory_73's source record this cycle — the archive budget is spent — so I'm treating it as directionally useful but unconfirmed, and I'm explicitly flagging downstream value risk: matching a competitor into a pricing war risks eroding margins, training the customer base toward price sensitivity, and attracting lower-LTV accounts, all of which cut against the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. To manage this without ignoring the urgent signal, I'm scoping this as a small_guarded_test — narrowly targeted at the specific at-risk price-sensitive SMB cohort showing elevated churn conversations, not a broad rollout — so we can observe retention and margin effects before any wider commitment, and so onboarding work can still be prioritized as next week's slot once this immediate threat is contained.
